subject: MedSync Health - implementation & routing plan

Subject: MedSync Health - implementation & routing plan

Hi Aaron / Emily —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + proposed next steps so engineering can start scoping: 

What we heard
- Primary workload: clinical note summarization + structured extraction, plus an embeddings index for search/clinician reranking.
- Data sensitivity: PHI in certain fields — security/compliance will be a gating item.
- Latency target: P95 <= 200ms for single-turn generation (critical on read path).
- Expected load: steady-state ~20 rps, peak bursts to 50 rps; batch jobs for nightly indexing.

Initial recommendations (high level)
1) Deployment mode: because of PHI, we should scope Redwood Private (VPC) with the option for Dedicated reserved GPU pools for steady throughput. If procurement requires hosted-only we can propose strict isolation + KMS — I'll confirm differences with Markus.
2) Model routing: propose primary cheaper LLM for most generation and a fallback higher-quality variant for complex cases. We can also send low-confidence outputs to a reranker that uses embeddings.
3) Auth & SDK: SDK quickstart uses API keys for initial PoC; for Private we recommend mTLS + signed JWTs. I'll attach a short SDK setup doc.
4) Structured output / tool calling: recommend using the structured output feature for extraction (JSON schema enforcement) and a toolkit integration for redaction/PII markers before indexing.

Action items / next steps
- I attached a 1-page SDK quickstart and a draft integration playbook — please confirm which network topology (VPC peering vs. PrivateLink) your infra prefers.
- Aaron / Emily: can you share a SOC2 scope PDF and a point of contact on security so we can size Private?
- We'll schedule a technical deep-dive next week (30–45 min) to align on routing policies and fallback thresholds.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md, redwood-integration-playbook.xlsx

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your constraints.

—Olga

- Latency: P95 < 200ms sounds right for the clinician read path; for batch summarization latency is less critical.
- Scale: 20 rps baseline, 50 rps peak is accurate; we may run larger spikes during peak triage windows but those are short.
- PHI: yes, our legal team needs Private deployment (VPC or on-prem). We can share the SOC2 scope (attached).
- Security contact: looping in Emily for infra/procurement next steps.

Two quick asks:
1) Can you sketch the minimal network diagram for Private + Dedicated GPUs (what ports, IP ranges, peering options)?
2) For model routing, we need a clear failover policy if the primary cheaper model fails quality checks — can Redwood do automatic fallback and tiered cost controls?

If you can send a short tech brief addressing the two asks above we can route to our secops and procurement. Also please include an initial ballpark for monthly committed spend for Dedicated (we'll need a budget placeholder).

Aaron — thanks for the SOC2 doc and the clarifying Qs. Below is a concise tech brief that you can hand to secops/procurement; happy to expand in the deep-dive.

Short tech brief (Private + Dedicated option)
1) Network & connectivity (minimal diagram attached)
   - Options: VPC peering (fast, simple) or AWS PrivateLink (recommended for cross-account isolation). For on-prem we'll support site-to-site VPN.
   - Required egress: outbound TLS to Redwood control plane (for management); inference traffic stays within customer's VPC for Private mode. We'll provide a small set of CIDR ranges and mTLS certs.
2) Auth and key management
   - PoC: API key scoped to project.
   - Production Private: mTLS + mutual auth to inference nodes, plus KMS for model encryption. We can integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS/HSM).
3) Model routing & policy (configurable rules)
   - Primary route: low-cost model (e.g., 4-bit quantized variant) for standard summaries.
   - Quality gate: confidence thresholds + heuristic checks (token-level perplexity / classification model) mark an output as low-quality.
   - Fallback chain: if flagged, call higher-capacity model variant (same architecture, larger or higher-precision weights) and run an embeddings-based reranker.
   - Cost controls: per-route cost caps + percentage-based downgrade windows (e.g., keep fallback capped at X% of calls per hour).
   - Latency policy: route-by-latency-SLO — prefer nodes in us-west for lowest p95, fallback to cross-region only when cost/availability dictates.
4) Structured output & tool-calling
   - Use structured output schemas for extraction (JSON schema enforcement) to reduce post-processing errors.
   - Implement a pre-processing redaction step (local) before sending to the model; tool-calls (e.g., lookup) can be executed by a safe sandbox and results stitched into the final JSON.
5) Embeddings / reranker
   - Embeddings indexed nightly; reranker uses a dense-sparse hybrid to surface clinical documents.
   - For tight latency constraints, run reranking asynchronously with tens-of-ms cached top-K results; synchronous rerank only for clinician-triggered queries.

Operational notes
- Canary rollouts: we'll recommend gradual rollouts with canary traffic split (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and automatic rollback on NPS/quality regressions.
- Observability: per-route token breakdown and per-model latency histograms; we'll provide an initial dashboard for the PoC.

Attachments: redwood-private-network-diagram.png, redwood-integration-playbook.xlsx

Cost placeholder (very rough)
- Private + Dedicated baseline: estimated $12k–$20k / month depending on instance family and replication. We will produce a formal quote after we finalize target model variants and throughput.

Next steps
- I'll schedule a 45-min architecture deep-dive (tentative slots next Tue/Wed).
- Markus will follow up with a short procurement checklist and a bill-of-materials for Dedicated capacity.

If you want, I can include a sample routing policy JSON in the deep-dive slide deck to make the fallback mechanics explicit.

—Olga

Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Olga — this looks good and addresses the main concerns. A couple quick items: 

- Procurement: please include the initial ballpark quote and a sample SOW template (we need those to open an internal PR).
- SecOps: we'll run your minimal network diagram by our security team; can you also provide the CIDR list and the mTLS certificate rotation schedule?
- Scheduling: next Tue 2/23 at 10:00 PT works for an architecture deep-dive — please send a calendar invite with dial-in and the deck.

On the routing policy: we want the fallback budget to be explicit (e.g., max 15% of total inference spend in any 1-hr window) and the ability to switch to a degraded-mode policy that prioritizes latency over quality during incident windows. Can your team prepare two short policy examples for the call?

Thanks — Emily
